My focus is on ensuring these values are handled exclusively by the database, as per the specified requirements, and not by client interactions.\n"[39m +

            },

              toolCallId: [32m'P4ZrB9R6aW4eCa7Z'[39m,

        {
          role: [32m'tool'[39m,
          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,
              toolCallId: [32m'P4ZrB9R6aW4eCa7Z'[39m,
              toolName: [32m'webSearch'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- We've given our schema declaration language syntax a sleek new makeover,\n"[39m +
                      [32m'replacing `->` with `:` and making `property` and `link` keywords\n'[39m +
                      [32m'optional.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- *Triggers* and *mutation rewrites* let you implement advanced validation and make the database *react* to your queries in interesting ways.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In short, `->` is replaced with the familiar `:` while `link` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`property` keywords become optional in most contexts.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As we are committed to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'maintaining backwards compatibility, the old syntax will be supported forever.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The result?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'EdgeQL got two new mechanisms: "Triggers" and "Mutation Rewrites".\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In essence, the distinction between the two is quite straightforward:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a *Trigger* cannot alter the object that activated it, but it can do pretty much anything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *Mutation Rewrite*, on the other hand, enables you to intercept mutating queries and rewrite them conditionally based on the old or new value, or even on what was specified precisely in the mutating query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`after` triggers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Triggers - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-03-07, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/triggers)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query type is run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Syntax ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This declaration defines a new trigger with the following options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **type-name**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The name (optionally module-qualified) of the type to be triggered on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **name**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The name of the trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **insert | update | delete [, ...]**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The query type (or types) to trigger on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple values with commas to invoke the same trigger for multiple types of queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If not, the trigger is skipped.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated when the trigger is invoked.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'alter type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'drop trigger name;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# v3.0 - Changelog | Resources\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-03-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/3_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Alternatively, specify an instance name if you aren't using a project.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Our new triggers feature is one of the most anticipated 3.0 features!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given query type is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The original query will *trigger* your pre-defined expression to run in a transaction along with the original query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These can be defined in your schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required name: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger log_insert after insert for each do (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'insert Log {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"action := 'insert',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'target_name := __new__.name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The trigger above inserts a `Log` object any time a `Person` object is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'inserted.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-04-05, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Syntax ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new mutation rewrite corresponding to the more explicit DDL commands.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites must be defined inside a property or link block.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This declaration defines a new trigger with the following options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **insert | update [, ...]**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The query type (or types) the rewrite runs on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple values with commas to invoke the same rewrite for multiple types of queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated to produce the new value of the property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new mutation rewrite.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When creating a new property or link:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create { property | link } prop-or-link-name: type "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}" ;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}" ;\n'[39m +

                      [32m'When altering an existing property or link:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2017-06-29, last updated: 2025-05-19, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel/blob/master/docs/intro/edgeql.rst)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'EdgeQL is the query language of Gel.\n'[39m +

          content: [
            {
              type: [32m'tool-result'[39m,

              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-01-01, last updated: 2025-01-11, [Read more](https://docs.edgedb.com/database/reference/sdl/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Declare two mutation rewrites: one that sets a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`created` property when a new\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object is inserted and one that sets a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`modified` property on each update:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert using (datetime_of_statement());\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite update using (datetime_of_statement());\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Syntax\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new mutation rewrite corresponding to the more explicit DDL commands.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites must be defined inside a property or link block.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This declaration defines a new trigger with the following options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- insert | update [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The query type (or types) the rewrite runs on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple values with commas to invoke the same rewrite for multiple types of queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated to produce the new value of the property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 Mutation Rewrites & Triggers- Audit logs, cached computeds, super constraints, and more!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-07-04, last updated: 2026-02-12, [Read more](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ImgMfb_jCJQ)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites and triggers are two complementary EdgeDB 3.0 features with tons of different uses.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Your database does stuff for you so your application doesn't have to!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'🤖 Track when an object is updated in a property on that same object with mutation rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🤖 Create detailed audit log records using triggers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🤖 Mutate values as they come into your database with mutation rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🤖 Make more flexible constraints by pairing triggers with the `assert` function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🤖 Cache computed values with mutation rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Learn more from our documentation:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'• Mutation rewrites- https://www.edgedb.com/docs/datamodel/mutation_rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{ts:21} by adding a mutation rewrite I can update the value automatically every time the object is mutated'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- *Triggers* and *mutation rewrites* let you implement advanced validation and make the database *react* to your queries in interesting ways.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The result?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'EdgeQL got two new mechanisms: "Triggers" and "Mutation Rewrites".\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Post {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required title: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required body: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'author: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'title_modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Only update `title_modified` if a new value\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# for `title` was specified in the query:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite update using (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'datetime_of_statement()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if __specified__.title\n'[39m +
                      [32m'else __old__.title_modified\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In essence, the distinction between the two is quite straightforward:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a *Trigger* cannot alter the object that activated it, but it can do pretty much anything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *Mutation Rewrite*, on the other hand, enables you to intercept mutating queries and rewrite them conditionally based on the old or new value, or even on what was specified precisely in the mutating query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`after` triggers.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Using a mutation rewrite as a better property default in the ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-29, last updated: 2025-10-03, [Read more](https://miroslavpetrik.medium.com/using-a-mutation-rewrite-as-a-better-default-property-in-the-edgedb-1c81b660368f)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A more powerful construct which allows us to hook into the database mutations are the mutation rewrites.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since we want to set the initial value, we can use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'insert\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Reservation { required price: float32 { rewrite insert using (.room.price * .daysCount); }}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Finally this gets the job done, but there is a catch — the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When we attempt to insert an Reservation, the client (CLI, or TypeScript) will require the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property, even though it will always get overwritten with the mutation rewrite:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'referencing the currently written values.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We can update the rewrite, so when an initial price is set in the insert query, it will be used instead of the computed value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Reservation { price: float32 { rewrite insert using (__subject__.price ?? (.room.price * .daysCount)); }}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note, that here we need to make the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property optional, so the client won’t require the price property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(Otherwise the computed default would never be used).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As it appears, the default has a precedence over the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# v4.0 - Changelog | Resources\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-03-12, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/4_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The directory name\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- Type check mutation rewrites at migration time\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(#6466)\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Mutation rewrite's `using` expression are now required to be of correct\n"[39m +
                      [32m'type when the rewrite is created.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Up until now, it was possible to migrate to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a schema that contained a rewrite rule that would always throw a type error\n'[39m +
                      [32m'when an object was being inserted or updated.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This might be considered a breaking change, but as it is clearly a bug in\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# GitHub - geldata/rfcs: RFCs for major changes to EdgeDB\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-01-28, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/rfcs)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- RFC 1020 - Triggers (accepted)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- RFC 1021 - Mutation rewrites (accepted)'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites - Introspection - Schema | Reference - Gel Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/introspection/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select schema::ObjectType {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'links: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'properties: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"} filter .name = 'schema::Rewrite';\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Introspection of all properties in the `default` schema with a mutation\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select schema::ObjectType {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'properties := (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select .properties {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrites: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'kind\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} filter exists .rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m"} filter .name ilike 'default::%'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'and exists .properties.rewrites;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Introspection of all rewrites, including the type of query (`kind`),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite expression, and the object and property they are on:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select schema::Rewrite {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'subject := (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select .subject {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'source: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'kind,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Introspection of all rewrites on a `default::Post` property named\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`modified`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'db>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select schema::Rewrite {kind, expr}\n'[39m +
                      [32m"filter .subject.source.name = 'default::Post'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"and .subject.name = 'modified';\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Any change to describe a default source for a property that sets a new value on an update? · geldata gel · Discussion #3180\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-11-12, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel/discussions/3180)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Currently, there isn't a schema-level way of implementing `updated_at` like you've described, so you'll need to keep including `updated_at := std::datetime_current()` in your `UPDATE` statements.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'We are working on a general query rewrite system (see roadmap), which would allow arbitrary injection of operations into queries based on a condition (or unconditionally).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We expect this (or some part of it) to land in 2.0.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Yes, though not for 2.0.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites were implemented in 3.0.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Feature-Request: Query/Mutation Hook Support · geldata gel · Discussion #3455\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-02-11, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel/discussions/3455)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Mutation Hooks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These hooks will trigger on insert/update/delete.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**They should also be able to modify/extend the users intentions by returning data to EdgeDB**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Following hooks will be needed to cover the mutation side of things:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Pre- Insert/Update/Delete Hooks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These hooks need to be called **before** data is added/updated/deleted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use-cases are:\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-04-05, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites allow you to intercept database mutations (i.e.,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'inserts and/or updates) and set the value of a property or link to the result of an expression you define.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new mutation rewrite corresponding to the more explicit DDL commands.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites must be defined inside a property or link block.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **insert | update [, ...]**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The query type (or types) the rewrite runs on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple values with commas to invoke the same rewrite for multiple types of queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated to produce the new value of the property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When creating a new property or link:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create { property | link } prop-or-link-name: type "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When altering an existing property or link:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'alter { property | link } prop-or-link-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}" ;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}" ;'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'abstract type Content {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required property title -> str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi link actors: Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property character_name -> str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In short, `->` is replaced with the familiar `:` while `link` and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`property` keywords become optional in most contexts.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In essence, the distinction between the two is quite straightforward:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a *Trigger* cannot alter the object that activated it, but it can do pretty much anything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *Mutation Rewrite*, on the other hand, enables you to intercept mutating queries and rewrite them conditionally based on the old or new value, or even on what was specified precisely in the mutating query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`after` triggers.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# v3.0 - Changelog | Resources\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-03-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/3_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You're no longer required to use the `property` or `link` keywords for\n"[39m +
                      [32m'non-computed properties and links.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Post {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required title: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required body: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert, update using (datetime_of_statement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This shows one reason mutation rewrites is one of our most wanted features:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified timestamps!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a user inserts or updates a `Post`, the rewrite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'will set the value of the `modified` property to that value of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`datetime_of_statement()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are tons of other uses too.'[39m

                      [32m'So we make the following change in the schema file:\n'[39m +

              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Post {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'author: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'title_modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Only update `title_modified` if a new value\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# for `title` was specified in the query:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite update using (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'datetime_of_statement()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if __specified__.title\n'[39m +
                      [32m'else __old__.title_modified\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required body: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'author: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'byline: str {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Cache computed byline on every update.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert, update using (\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'by ' ++\n"[39m +
                      [32m'__subject__.author ++\n'[39m +
                      [32m"' on ' ++\n"[39m +
                      [32m"to_str(__subject__.created, 'Mon DD, YYYY')\n"[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In essence, the distinction between the two is quite straightforward:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a *Trigger* cannot alter the object that activated it, but it can do pretty much anything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *Mutation Rewrite*, on the other hand, enables you to intercept mutating queries and rewrite them conditionally based on the old or new value, or even on what was specified precisely in the mutating query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`after` triggers.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-01-01, last updated: 2025-01-11, [Read more](https://docs.edgedb.com/database/reference/sdl/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Declare two mutation rewrites: one that sets a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`created` property when a new\n'[39m +
                      [32m'object is inserted and one that sets a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`modified` property on each update:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert using (datetime_of_statement());\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite update using (datetime_of_statement());\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new mutation rewrite corresponding to the more explicit DDL commands.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites must be defined inside a property or link block.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This declaration defines a new trigger with the following options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- insert | update [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The query type (or types) the rewrite runs on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple values with commas to invoke the same rewrite for multiple types of queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated to produce the new value of the property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Using a mutation rewrite as a better property default in the ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-29, last updated: 2025-10-03, [Read more](https://miroslavpetrik.medium.com/using-a-mutation-rewrite-as-a-better-default-property-in-the-edgedb-1c81b660368f)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A more powerful construct which allows us to hook into the database mutations are the mutation rewrites.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since we want to set the initial value, we can use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'insert\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Finally this gets the job done, but there is a catch — the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When we attempt to insert an Reservation, the client (CLI, or TypeScript) will require the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property, even though it will always get overwritten with the mutation rewrite:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'referencing the currently written values.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We can update the rewrite, so when an initial price is set in the insert query, it will be used instead of the computed value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Reservation { price: float32 { rewrite insert using (__subject__.price ?? (.room.price * .daysCount)); }}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note, that here we need to make the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property optional, so the client won’t require the price property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(Otherwise the computed default would never be used).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This could break the UI, because now querying the property will return\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'value, but no luck here.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As it appears, the default has a precedence over the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# v3.0 - Changelog | Resources\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-03-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/3_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The mutation rewrites feature is the sibling, or at least the first cousin, of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'triggers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Both are automatically invoked when a write operation occurs on the\n'[39m +
                      [32m"type they're on, but triggers are not able to make changes to the object that\n"[39m +
                      [32m'invoked them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites are built to do just that!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required body: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert, update using (datetime_of_statement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This shows one reason mutation rewrites is one of our most wanted features:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified timestamps!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a user inserts or updates a `Post`, the rewrite\n'[39m +

                      [32m'There are tons of other uses too.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Give them a try!\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The support of version pre-1.0 binary protocol is deprecated in EdgeDB 3.0, and\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 Mutation Rewrites & Triggers- Audit logs, cached computeds, super constraints, and more!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-07-04, last updated: 2026-02-12, [Read more](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ImgMfb_jCJQ)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites and triggers are two complementary EdgeDB 3.0 features with tons of different uses.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Insert\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-01-18, [Read more](https://docs.edgedb.com/tutorial/data-mutations/insert/insert-result)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You may have noticed that when you run an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`insert` command,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'some data is returned as the result.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Every\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# RFC 1011: Policy based query rewrite by elprans · Pull Request #50 · edgedb/rfcs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-01-18, [Read more](https://github.com/edgedb/rfcs/pull/50/files)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Agree.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It does.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Read queries with mutating policies are considered mutations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All policies will get compiled into affected queries.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +

                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-04-05, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites allow you to intercept database mutations (i.e.,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'inserts and/or updates) and set the value of a property or link to the result of an expression you define.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'in the mutation.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'modified: datetime {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'if <json>__subject__ {**} != <json>__old__ {**}\n'[39m +

                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites must be defined inside a property or link block.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'We can update the rewrite, so when an initial price is set in the insert query, it will be used instead of the computed value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Reservation { price: float32 { rewrite insert using (__subject__.price ?? (.room.price * .daysCount)); }}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note, that here we need to make the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property optional, so the client won’t require the price property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(Otherwise the computed default would never be used).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This could break the UI, because now querying the property will return\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As it appears, the default has a precedence over the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# v3.0 - Changelog | Resources - Gel Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-03-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/3_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Mutation rewrites ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The mutation rewrites feature is the sibling, or at least the first cousin, of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'triggers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Both are automatically invoked when a write operation occurs on the\n'[39m +
                      [32m"type they're on, but triggers are not able to make changes to the object that\n"[39m +
                      [32m'invoked them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites are built to do just that!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Post {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required title: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required body: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified: datetime {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite insert, update using (datetime_of_statement())\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This shows one reason mutation rewrites is one of our most wanted features:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'modified timestamps!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a user inserts or updates a `Post`, the rewrite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'will set the value of the `modified` property to that value of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`datetime_of_statement()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are tons of other uses too.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Give them a try!'[39m
                  },

                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites - Introspection - Schema | Reference - Gel Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/introspection/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'links: {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and exists .properties.rewrites;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Introspection of all rewrites, including the type of query (`kind`),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite expression, and the object and property they are on:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'......\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'subject := (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select .subject {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'source: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'kind,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I'm currently deep in thought about the precise implementation of versioning for our data objects. The core requirement is to increment the `version` field by one after every successful `update`, ensuring it's always one greater than the prior state. The initial insertion will set it to `1`.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Defining Data Timestamps**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I'm now considering the precise definition and behavior of `created_at` and `modified_at` fields. `created_at` should be immutable upon insertion, reflecting the statement timestamp, while `modified_at` will capture the timestamp of each update operation, ensuring accurate temporal tracking.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Implementing Denormalization**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I'm currently grappling with the intricacies of denormalizing the parent `document_slug` onto the `Comment` object. My thoughts are focused on ensuring this field is automatically populated on insert and correctly updates when a comment's associated document changes, all while ignoring client-provided values. I'm validating how mutation rewrites will handle this.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Designing Audit Entry**\n'[39m +

                [32m'I am now focusing on the design of the `AuditEntry` object, specifically its properties like `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, and `version`. My next step is to consider how triggers and rules will populate this, linking it to our auditing requirements.\n'[39m +

The `version` should reflect the object's state at the time of the mutation, and `at` must be consistent across all entries generated by a single statement, including the exact `created_at` or `modified_at` value applied.\n"[39m +

My focus is on ensuring each operation generates a single `AuditEntry`, and that deletion cascades correctly trigger audits for associated comments.\n"[39m +

              output: {
                type: [32m'content'[39m,
                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required name: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger log_update after update for each do (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'insert AuditLog {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"action := 'update',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'target_name := __new__.name,\n'[39m +
                      [32m"change := __old__.name ++ '->' ++ __new__.name\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In essence, the distinction between the two is quite straightforward:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a *Trigger* cannot alter the object that activated it, but it can do pretty much anything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *Mutation Rewrite*, on the other hand, enables you to intercept mutating queries and rewrite them conditionally based on the old or new value, or even on what was specified precisely in the mutating query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`after` triggers.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Triggers - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-03-07, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/triggers)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query type is run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The original query will *trigger* your pre-defined expression to run in a transaction along with the original query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression will be evaluted once for the entire query, even if multiple objects were modified.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`__new__` and `__old__` in this context within the expression refer to sets of the modified objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Added in v4.0- **when (condition)**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Optionally provide a condition for the trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the condition is met, the trigger will run.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If not, the trigger is skipped.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated when the trigger is invoked.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new trigger.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create trigger name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'after\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{insert | update | delete} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    for {each | all}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[ when (condition) ]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'do expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}"'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Gel: edb/tools/pygments/edgeql/meta.py\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-03-29, [Read more](https://fossies.org/linux/gel/edb/tools/pygments/edgeql/meta.py)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m''[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# gel/docs/resources/changelog/3_x.rst at master · geldata/gel\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2017-06-29, last updated: 2025-06-12, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel/blob/master/docs/resources/changelog/3_x.rst)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Our new triggers feature is one of the most anticipated 3.0 features! Triggers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given query type is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'run on an object type. The original query will *trigger* your pre-defined expression to run in a transaction along with the original query. These can be defined in your schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  required name: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  trigger log_insert after insert for each do (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    insert Log {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"      action := 'insert',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'      target_name := __new__.name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  );\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mutation rewrites - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-04-05, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/mutation_rewrites)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites allow you to intercept database mutations (i.e.,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'inserts and/or updates) and set the value of a property or link to the result of an expression you define.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'  using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Mutation rewrites must be defined inside a property or link block.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This declaration defines a new trigger with the following options:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **insert | update [, ...]**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The query type (or types) the rewrite runs on.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate multiple values with commas to invoke the same rewrite for multiple types of queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **expr**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The expression to be evaluated to produce the new value of the property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define a new mutation rewrite.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When creating a new property or link:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create { property | link } prop-or-link-name: type "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      using expr\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"}" ;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When altering an existing property or link:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{create | alter} type type-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'alter { property | link } prop-or-link-name "{"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create rewrite {insert | update} [, ...]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'      using expr'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# CHANGELOG.md - Hex Preview\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Gel\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-04, last updated: 2026-07-27, [Read more](https://dbdb.io/db/gel)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In February 2025, EdgeDB was renamed to Gel.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Projects - Using Gel | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-04, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/using/projects)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Hooks are divided into two categories: `before` and `after` as indicated\n'[39m +
                      [32m'by their names.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All of the `before` hooks are executed prior to their\n'[39m +
                      [32m'corresponding commands, so they happen before any changes are made.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All of the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`after` hooks run after the CLI command and thus the effects from the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'command are already in place.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- gel project init command triggers the `project.init.before`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and `project.init.after` hook.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the migrations are applied at the end of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the initialization, then the `migration.apply.before`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`schema.update.before`, `migration.apply.after`, and\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`schema.update.after` hooks are also triggered.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- gel branch switch command triggers `branch.switch.before`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`schema.update.before`, `branch.switch.after`, and `schema.update.after`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'hooks in that relative order.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- gel branch wipe command triggers the `branch.wipe.before`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`schema.update.before`, `branch.wipe.after`, and `schema.update.after`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'hooks in that relative order.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- gel migration apply command triggers `migration.apply.before`, `schema.update.before`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`migration.apply.after`, and `schema.update.after` hooks in that\n'[39m +
                      [32m'relative order.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# gel-js/docs/reference.rst at master · geldata/gel-js\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2015-09-13, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel-js/blob/master/docs/reference.rst)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The client automatically converts EdgeDB types to the corresponding JavaScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'types and vice versa.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The table below shows the correspondence between EdgeDB and JavaScript types.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'|`anytuple`|`Array`|\n'[39m +

                      [32m'|`Object`|`object`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`bool`|`boolean`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`bytes`|`Uint8Array`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`str`|`string`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`float32`, `float64`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`|`number`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`bigint`|`BigInt`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`decimal`|n/a|'[39m
                  },

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# JSON - Standard Library | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-29, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/stdlib/json)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'JSON in Gel is a scalar type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This type doesn't have its own literal, and instead can be obtained by either casting a value to the `json` type, or by using the `to_json()` function:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Any value in Gel can be cast to a `json` type as well:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `json_object_pack()` function provides one more way to construct JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It constructs a JSON object from an array of key/value tuples:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Additionally, any `Object` in Gel can be cast as a `json` type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This produces the same JSON value as the JSON-serialized result of that said object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Furthermore, this result will be the same as the output of a `select expression` in *JSON mode*, including the shape of that type:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Instead, use the `to_str()` function to dump a JSON value to a `str` value.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use the `to_json()` function to parse a JSON string to a `json` value:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'std::json_object_pack(pairs: SET OF tuple<str, json>) -> json'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 1.0 Alpha 1 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2019-04-11, last updated: 2025-02-26, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-1-0-alpha-1)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Working with JSON in EdgeQL is a breeze: any type or a lexical structure can be cast into JSON, no matter how complex, flat, or nested it is.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This makes it simple to construct JSON objects in your queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The example below casts named tuples and arrays of them to JSON:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'edgedb>\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# General documentation update · Issue #39 · geldata/gel\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Named tuples can now be indexed by position.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The below two queries are equivalent:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to access tuple property with dynamic key in Gel (EdgeDB)?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-03-03, last updated: 2025-05-22, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79476615/how-to-access-tuple-property-with-dynamic-key-in-gel-edgedb)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I came up with a way by casting the tuple to JSON, and then using\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'json_get\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m':\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'with lng := $lng\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select <str>json_get(<json>(pl := "bober", en:= "beaver"), lng))));\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Also, I was able to constrain the keys by going through a function, to make sure only valid calls are made:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'scalar type Lang extending str {\n'[39m +
                      [32m`constraint one_of("pl", 'en');\n`[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function get_tuple_lang(tpl: tuple<pl: str, en: str>, lng: Lang) -> str\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using (assert_exists(assert_single(<str>json_get(<json>tpl, lng))));\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This works:'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Literals - EdgeQL | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/edgeql/literals)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Optionally, you can assign a key to each element of a tuple.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These are known\n'[39m +
                      [32m'as *named tuples*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `json` scalar type is a stringified representation of structured data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'JSON literals are declared by explicitly casting other values or passing a properly formatted JSON string into `to_json()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Any type can be converted into JSON except `bytes`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'select <json>(name := "named tuple", count := 2);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'db>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`select to_json('{"a": 2, "b": 5}');\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`{'{"a": 2, "b": 5}'}\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'JSON values support indexing operators.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The resulting value is also of type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`json`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`select to_json('{"a": 2, "b": 5}')['a'];\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`select to_json('["a", "b", "c"]')[2];\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Indexing|`json[i]` `json[from:to]` `json[name]` `json_get()`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Merging|`json ++ json`|'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeQL | Learn\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 1999-03-31, last updated: 2026-03-12, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/learn/edgeql)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'e.tuple({fruit: "Apple", quantity: 3.14, fresh: true});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'e.json(["this", "is", "an", "array"]);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// unknown\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Gel also supports a special `json` type for representing unstructured\n'[39m +
                      [32m'data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Primitive data structures can be converted to JSON using a type cast\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(`<json>`).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Alternatively, a properly JSON-encoded string can be converted\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to `json` with the built-in `to_json` function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Indexing a `json` value\n'[39m +
                      [32m'returns another `json` value.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'gel>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`select to_json('[{ "name": "Peter Parker" }]');\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'gel>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`select to_json('[{ "name": "Peter Parker" }]')[0]['name'];\n`[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'/*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The result of an query returning `json` is represented\n'[39m +
                      [32m'with `unknown` in TypeScript.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Access Dynamic Tuple Properties in EdgeDB Using json_get\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-12-19, last updated: 2026-01-20, [Read more](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CE-SooxNtnw)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Learn how to dynamically access tuple properties in EdgeDB's GEL query language by casting tuples to JSON and safely handling keys with scalar constraints.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Solution: Cast Tuple to JSON and Use json_get\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can work around this by converting the tuple to a JSON object, which does support dynamic key access:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[[See Video to Reveal this Text or Code Snippet]]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Here’s what happens:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The tuple (pl: str, en: str) is cast to a JSON object.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'json_get(json_obj, key) retrieves the value dynamically.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Cast the result back to str.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This approach gives you safe dynamic tuple property access.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Summary\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Tuples in EdgeDB cannot be indexed by dynamic keys directly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Casting tuples to JSON allows dynamic property access with json_get.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Constrain dynamic keys with a custom scalar type for safety.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This method balances flexibility and type safety in EdgeDB queries involving dynamic tuple property access, perfect for i18n or similar use cases.'[39m
                  },

                    text: [32m'# 1.0 Alpha 5\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-03-23, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/1_0_a5)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Implement casts between JSON and enums, arrays and tuples (#251).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For example, now there's a way to unpack JSON input into a tuple, which can then be used to populate a new User record:Copy\n"[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
