                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Implement support for link target deletion policy · Issue #239 · edgedb/edgedb\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2018-10-04, last updated: 2024-10-09, [Read more](https://github.com/edgedb/edgedb/issues/239)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# eschema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Foo:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'link bar -> Spam:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on target delete: <action>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# DDL:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'CREATE TYPE Foo CREATE LINK bar -> Spam ON TARGET DELETE <action>;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Where is one of the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'DELETE SOURCE\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The actions have no inherent "weight", and are equal and mutually exclusive.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Foo\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'No, if orphan is syntax, arbitrary expressions are not allowed currently.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The proposed declaration syntax is as follows:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Where is one of the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`RESTRICT`-- produce an error indicating that deletion cannot be done due to an existing link.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is the default.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`DEFERRED RESTRICT`-- same as the above, but the check is postponed until the end of the current transaction, if there is no transaction, equivalent to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`SET EMPTY`-- remove the link, can only be used with links that are not\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`required`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`SET DEFAULT`-- remove the link, and replace it with links pointing to the objects returned by the default expression, if the default expression returns an empty set, and the link is required, an error is produced,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`DELETE SOURCE`-- remove the link and the source of the link (cascaded deletion).'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Delete - EdgeQL | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-11, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/edgeql/delete)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Every link is associated with a *link deletion policy*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"By default, it isn't possible to delete an object linked to by another.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To avoid this behavior, we could update the `Movie.characters` link to use\n'[39m +
                      [32m'the `allow` deletion policy.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Movie {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required title: str { constraint exclusive };\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required release_year: int64;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi characters: Person;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi characters: Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on target delete allow;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Cascading deletes ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If a link uses the `delete source` policy, then deleting a *target* of the link will also delete the object that links to it (the *source*).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This behavior can be used to implement cascading deletes; be careful with this power!'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB v2 (Sagittarius).mdCopy page\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-29, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/2_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Take your application offline, then dump your v1.x database with the CLI\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'gel dump --dsn <old dsn> --all my_database.dump/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The file name isn't\n"[39m +
                      [32m'important.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Restore the empty v2.x instance from the dump\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'gel restore --all my_database.dump/ --dsn <new dsn>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once the restore is complete, update your application to connect to the new\n'[39m +
                      [32m'instance.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Source deletion policies ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Add deletion cascade functionality with `on source delete`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type BlogPost {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'property title -> str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi link posts -> BlogPost {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on source delete delete target;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Under this policy, deleting a `User` will unconditionally delete its\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`posts` as well.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To avoid deleting a `Post` that is linked to by other schema entities,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'append `if orphan`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi link posts -> BlogPost {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on source delete delete target;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on source delete delete target if orphan;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Links - Schema | Reference\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-22, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/reference/datamodel/links)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Target deletion ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The clause `on target delete` determines the action when the target object is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'deleted:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `restrict` (default) — raises an exception if the target is deleted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `delete source` — deletes the source when the target is deleted (a cascade).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `allow` — removes the target from the link if the target is deleted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `deferred restrict` — like `restrict` but defers the error until the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'end of the transaction if the object remains linked.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Source deletion ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The clause `on source delete` determines the action when the **source** is deleted:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `allow` — deletes the source, removing the link to the target.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `delete target` — unconditionally deletes the target as well.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- `delete target if orphan` — deletes the target if and only if it's no\n"[39m +
                      [32m'longer linked by any other object *via the same link*.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You can add `if orphan` if you'd like to avoid deleting a target that remains\n"[39m +
                      [32m'linked elsewhere via the **same** link name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `on target delete <action>` and `on source delete <action>` specify\n'[39m +
                      [32m'deletion policies.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `alter type ...'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# README.md\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-11-03, [Read more](http://www.git2pdf.com/public/edgedb.edgedb.2022-02-10T20:14:06.247Z.pdf)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'deleted, there are 4 possible *actions* that can be taken:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- ``restrict`` (default) - Any attempt to delete the target object im\n'[39m +
                      [32m'mediately\n'[39m +
                      [32m'raises an exception.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- ``delete source`` - when the target of a link is deleted, the sourc\n'[39m +
                      [32m'e\n'[39m +
                      [32m'is also deleted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is useful for implementing cascading deletes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The ``delete`` command is used to delete objects from the database.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Delete policy checker for humans · edgedb edgedb · Discussion #5057\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-02-17, last updated: 2025-01-08, [Read more](https://github.com/edgedb/edgedb/discussions/5057)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So with recently added\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`delete source`target deletion policy, it now possible to easily define deletion policies that work both ways (source to target, target to source) and when something becomes easier we tend to use it more.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Edgedb back reference one to many links to limit choices ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-11-10, last updated: 2025-03-22, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74387926/edgedb-back-reference-one-to-many-links-to-limit-choices-on-queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi link address -> Address{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'constraint exclusive;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on target delete delete source;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi link phone -> Phone{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on target delete delete source;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'link in_user -> User{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on target delete delete source;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'link in_worker -> Worker{'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# [Day06] - 如何delete - iT 邦幫忙::一起幫忙解決難題，拯救 IT 人的一天\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-19, last updated: 2026-03-29, [Read more](https://ithelp.ithome.com.tw/articles/10350544)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`deletion police`可以分為`target deletion`及`source deletion`兩種。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'其中`target deletion`有：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `restrict`（預設）。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `delete source`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `allow`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `deferred restrict`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'而`source deletion`有：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `allow`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `delete target`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `delete target if orphan`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### on target delete delete source\n'[39m +
                      [32m'此時如果將`delete policy`改為`on target delete delete source`：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required name: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi followers: User {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on target delete delete source;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'這個`deletion police`是指當有一個`User object`連接到其它`User object`的`multi followers link`時，如果這個`User object`被刪除的話，與其連接的`User object`也會被刪除。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'此時我們可以刪除`John`：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'delete User filter .name="John";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'on source delete delete target;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'此時我們可以刪除`Jeff`：'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Introduction to EdgeDB\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This means when a user is deleted, all their todo items are deleted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…'[39m

                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Exceptions Overhaul · geldata gel · Discussion #1849\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-10-01, last updated: 2025-05-24, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel/discussions/1849)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Adding a way to raise exceptions from EdgeQL.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We propose to add a new "throw" clause to EdgeQL allowing users to raise exceptions; example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"SELECT THROW errors::RuntimeUserError { message := 'something went wrong' };\n"[39m +
                      [32m'# or equivalent short version (always raises `RuntimeUserError`):\n'[39m +
                      [32m"SELECT THROW 'something went wrong';\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'raise EdgeQLSyntaxError(..., location=...)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# v3.0 - Changelog | Resources\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-03-13, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/3_x)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Our new triggers feature is one of the most anticipated 3.0 features!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Triggers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'allow you to define an expression to be executed whenever a given query type is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'run on an object type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The original query will *trigger* your pre-defined expression to run in a transaction along with the original query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These can be defined in your schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger log_insert after insert for each do (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'insert Log {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'target_name := __new__.name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The trigger above inserts a `Log` object any time a `Person` object is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'inserted.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The new `assert` function lets you do handy things like create powerful\n'[39m +
                      [32m'constraints when paired with triggers:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Copy\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'type Person {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required name: str;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi friends: Person;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'multi enemies: Person;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'trigger prohibit_frenemies after insert, update for each do (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'assert(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'not exists (__new__.friends intersect __new__.enemies),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'message := "Invalid frenemies",\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'edgedb error: EdgeDBError: Invalid frenemies\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use it in other contexts too — any time you want to throw an error when\n'[39m +
                      [32m"things don't go as planned."[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# EdgeDB 3.0 | Gel Blog\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-06-22, last updated: 2026-06-16, [Read more](https://www.geldata.com/blog/edgedb-3-0)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In essence, the distinction between the two is quite straightforward:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a *Trigger* cannot alter the object that activated it, but it can do pretty much anything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A *Mutation Rewrite*, on the other hand, enables you to intercept mutating queries and rewrite them conditionally based on the old or new value, or even on what was specified precisely in the mutating query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"To put it in SQL terms, EdgeDB's mutation rewrites correspond to SQL's `before` triggers, while EdgeDB's triggers align with SQL's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`after` triggers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- The new `assert()` function allows for custom descriptive errors from\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queries, functions, or triggers.'[39m
                  },

                    text: [32m'# 1.0 Beta 3\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-05-02, [Read more](https://docs.geldata.com/resources/changelog/1_0_b3)\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# GitHub - geldata/gel-python: The official Python client library for EdgeDB\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# rfcs/text/1000-migrations.rst at master · geldata/rfcs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-01-28, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/rfcs/blob/master/text/1000-migrations.rst)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Each migration has a unique name that is a hash derived from the token\n'[39m +
                      [32m'stream of the migration script and the migration parent name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`'m'`.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The names of the migrations are computed by the `edgedb migrate` command\n'[39m +
                      [32m'starting from the latest committed migration (if any), using the following\n'[39m +
                      [32m'algorithm:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Get the latest migration id from the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Scans all files in the migrations dir and finds a file that references\n'[39m +
                      [32m'that parent.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"3. If there's no such file --- terminate: there's no in-progress migration.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"4. if there's one such file and it has the largest sequential file name --\n"[39m +
                      [32m"then there's only one in-progress migration file, so it is committed.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the user modifies 0005.edgeql and runs edgedb migration commit,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'we first commit the 0004, validate that 0005 has the correct parent\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name, and if needed we fix it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We also compute it's new name, and then\n"[39m +
                      [32m'commit 00005.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This RFC makes no special\n'[39m +
                      [32m'provision as to the recovery from this situation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The user will either\n'[39m +
                      [32m'have to revert the migration file alteration, or reset the migration history\n'[39m +
                      [32m'with `RESET SCHEMA`.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# gel/docs/resources/changelog/3_x.rst at master · geldata/gel\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2017-06-29, last updated: 2025-06-12, [Read more](https://github.com/geldata/gel/blob/master/docs/resources/changelog/3_x.rst)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To upgrade a local project, first ensure that your CLI is up to date with\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'edgedb cli upgrade\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. Then run the following command inside the project\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ edgedb project upgrade\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Alternatively, specify an instance name if you aren't using a project.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$ edgedb instance upgrade -I my_instance\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You might also receive a different error which indicates the issue is within\n'[39m +
                      [32m'your migrations. In this case, the error can be fixed by squashing, as\n'[39m +
                      [32m'indicated by the error:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The current schema is compatible. But some of the migrations are outdated.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Please squash all migrations to fix the issue:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'   ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'   ```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This hash can be read and used to determine if a given query has changed and needs to be re-generated.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To upgrade a local project, run the following command inside the project\n'[39m +
                      [32m'directory.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'edgedb project upgrade --to-latest -I my_instance\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Hosted instances**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To upgrade a remote (hosted) instance, we recommend the following\n'[39m +
                      [32m'dump-and-restore process.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Spin up an empty 2.0 instance by following one of our deployment guides.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These guides have been updated to 2.0.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Keep the DSN of the newly created instance handy.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Take your application offline, then dump your v1.x database with the CLI\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once the restore is complete, update your application to connect to the new\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                [32m"I've realized the Gel CLI intelligently detects altered migration files by comparing hashes. It then conveniently provides the correct, updated hash, streamlining the correction process.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use listFiles to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Command Execution:\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - cd "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct)\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'  - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)\n'[39m +
            [32m"- You shall avoid use the markdown code block syntax (backtick, '`') in your command, as it will be interpreted as a command substitution.\n"[39m +

You must also consider if the command you need to run should be executed in a specific directory rather than the current working directory, and properly set the `cwd` if necessary.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +

Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +

            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
